identity.title: ITBench: Evaluating AI Agents across Diverse Real-World IT Automation Tasks

problem.claim: Measure and understand how effectively AI agents perform critical real-world IT automation tasks.

gap.claim: The abstract identifies a need for systematic benchmarking methodology for AI-agent IT automation.

contributions.claim: Introduces ITBench, a systematic framework for benchmarking AI agents on real-world IT automation tasks.
Provides 102 initial scenarios spanning SRE, CISO, and FinOps, designed for community extension, with a leaderboard and sample agent implementations.
Uses push-button workflows and interpretable metrics to characterize challenges and opportunities in IT automation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present ITBench as a systematic, extensible benchmark covering three IT-operations domains with operational workflows and interpretable metrics.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that state-of-the-art-model agents resolve 11.4% of SRE scenarios, 25.2% of CISO scenarios, and 25.8% of FinOps scenarios, excluding anomaly detection.
For FinOps anomaly-detection scenarios, the authors report an F1 score of 0.35.

narrative_sequence.summary: Effective AI-agent automation requires ways to measure and understand performance on critical IT tasks.
The authors introduce ITBench as a systematic benchmarking methodology for real-world IT automation.
The initial release covers SRE, CISO, and FinOps, using push-button workflows, interpretable metrics, and 102 extensible scenarios.
Agents resolve a minority of scenarios across the three domains; FinOps anomaly detection reaches an F1 of 0.35.
The benchmark, leaderboard, and sample implementations are released publicly; the authors position ITBench as an enabler of correct, safe, and fast automation.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a benchmark's operational interface and interpretable metrics with domain-specific scenario coverage and concrete resolution rates.

lessons.interpretation: A benchmark contribution is more informative when its scope, interaction workflow, metrics, and baseline outcomes are stated together.
lessons.application: Frame an evaluation resource by naming its target domains, scenario count, user workflow, metric interpretability, and representative baseline results.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the work is purely theoretical or when benchmark scope and evaluation metrics are not yet defined.

unknowns: The abstract does not define scenario construction, resolution criteria, model configurations, or evaluation protocols.
The conditions behind the reported rates and the FinOps anomaly-detection F1 are unspecified.
The claims that automation will be correct, safe, and fast are expectations, not reported validation results.
